title: Reading the Stay Statement: Amount of the Level-Change Credit on an Assisted Living Respite Stay
content:
On the statement of an Assisted Living Respite Stay under the Respite and Short-Term Stay Agreement, the level-change credit equals the re-leveled nights times the price charged per night by the segment being re-leveled, and it references that segment.

## The quantities, defined

- **The segment being re-leveled** is the stay's latest nightly charge segment, latest by posting date. It is the one nightly charge entry with the basis, the first night and the stay type billed of that latest nightly charge segment, so a segment that merely ends on the same night is never part of it.
- **The price charged per night by the segment being re-leveled** is that segment's amount divided by its nights. It is taken as it results from that division, without rounding.
- **The re-leveled nights** run from the level effective date on the stay through the last night of the segment being re-leveled, both nights counted.
- **The level-change credit** is the re-leveled nights multiplied by the price charged per night, rounded half up to the cent once, on the final product. Its nights are the re-leveled nights.

## Worked statements (hypothetical stays)

**Statement 1.** A hypothetical stay carries a planned-stay segment of 14 nights, first night 1 May, last night 14 May, amount 3,346.00. The price charged per night is 3,346.00 divided by 14, that is 239.00. The level effective date on the stay is 6 May, so the re-leveled nights run from 6 May through 14 May, both counted: 9 nights. The credit is 9 times 239.00, that is 2,151.00, for 9 nights, referencing the planned-stay segment.

**Statement 2.** A hypothetical stay's latest nightly charge segment is an entry of 13 nights, last night 20 June, amount 3,100.00. The price charged per night is 3,100.00 divided by 13, that is 238.461538 and so on. The level effective date is 16 June, so the re-leveled nights are 16 to 20 June, both counted: 5 nights. The product is 5 times 238.461538…, that is 1,192.307692…, and rounding once, half up to the cent, gives a credit of 1,192.31 for 5 nights.

**Statement 3.** A hypothetical stay has a planned-stay segment ending on 30 July and a later-posted extension segment whose first night is 31 July and whose last night is 9 August. The segment being re-leveled is the extension segment alone; the planned-stay segment is not part of it.

## Points of reading

| Question about the credit | Answer from the definitions above |
|---|---|
| Which entry does the credit reference? | The segment being re-leveled |
| Is the per-night price rounded before multiplying? | No; only the final product is rounded |
| Are the level effective date and the segment's last night both counted? | Yes, both are counted |
| What nights does the credit state? | The re-leveled nights |
